title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives Election in Arizona's 9th Congressional District
description: Arizona's 9th Congressional District covers western Arizona, including all of La Paz County, most of Mohave and Yuma Counties, and western portions of Maricopa County. With a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+15, it is the most Republican district in Arizona. Incumbent Republican Paul Gosar is seeking his ninth term in Congress. Democrat Danielle Sterbinsky, a Navy veteran and academic counselor, is challenging him. The Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid R' and the primary elections are scheduled for July 21, 2026.

candidates.name: Paul Gosar
candidates.summary: Paul Gosar is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Arizona's 9th Congressional District, first elected in 2010. A former dentist who owned his own practice in Flagstaff for 25 years, he is known as a staunch fiscal and social conservative who focuses on border security, cutting government spending, and opposing what he calls 'woke ideology'. He was censured by the House in 2021 for posting an animated video depicting violence against fellow lawmakers, but was later reinstated to committee assignments when Republicans regained the majority.

career_history.title: U.S. Representative
career_history.description: Representing Arizona's 1st, 4th, and now 9th congressional districts. Serves on House Natural Resources Committee and House Oversight and Government Reform Committee.

career_history.title: Dentist / Small Business Owner
career_history.description: Owned and operated a dental practice in Flagstaff, Arizona for 25 years. Named Arizona Dental Association Dentist of the Year in 2001.

candidates.name: Danielle Sterbinsky
candidates.summary: Danielle 'Dani' Sterbinsky is a Democratic candidate challenging incumbent Paul Gosar for Arizona's 9th Congressional District seat. A U.S. Navy veteran who served as an Operations Specialist on the USS Bainbridge, she holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Hawaii and a master's degree in industrial organizational psychology from Grand Canyon University. She works as an academic counselor at Grand Canyon University and has served on the Surprise Personnel Appeals Board, campaigning on affordability, housing stability, healthcare access, and fully funding public schools.
